Below is a *generic* outline for preparing a psychoactive test solution (here illustrated with caffeine, a legally available stimulant often used in human‐behavior studies).  You should adapt every step to your institution’s SOPs, applicable regulations (GMP, GLP), and your IRB/ethics approval.

1. Context of use  
   • Application: single‐blind or double‐blind, placebo-controlled studies of attention, reaction time, mood or vigilance.  
   • Typical human dose range: 2–5 mg/kg (e.g. 140 mg for a 70 kg volunteer), administered orally as a drink or in capsules.  

2. Materials & sourcing  
   • Pharmaceutical-grade anhydrous caffeine (≥ 99% purity) with CoA from a certified supplier.  
   • Sterile purified water or physiological saline.  
   • Analytical balance (± 0.1 mg) and calibrated volumetric glassware.  
   • 0.22 µm syringe filters and sterile amber vials.  

3. Preparation procedure (summarized)  
   a. Wearing lab coat, gloves and safety goggles, tare a weighing boat on the balance.  
   b. Weigh out the exact amount of caffeine to make your target stock (e.g. 1.0 g for a 100 mL stock at 10 mg/mL).  
   c. Transfer powder into a beaker, add ~80 mL sterile water, stir on a magnetic plate until fully dissolved.  
   d. Rinse vessel walls with additional water to bring to final volume (100 mL).  
   e. Draw solution into sterile syringe, pass through a 0.22 µm filter into a pre-labeled amber vial.  
   f. Label with concentration, date, preparer’s initials and storage conditions (2–8 °C).  

4. Safety & quality-control checks  
   • Consult and follow the SDS for caffeine: dust inhalation hazards, eye/skin irritation.  
   • Perform all weighing and dissolutions in a ventilated hood or low-dust area.  
   • Use PPE: nitrile gloves, eye protection, lab coat; change gloves if contaminated.  
   • Verify final concentration by UV-Vis or HPLC assay against a certified standard.  
   • Document batch records, retain CoA, and dispose of any waste as chemical hazardous waste.  

5. Human-subject safeguards  
   • Obtain prior IRB/ethics committee approval, informed consent, and clinical trial registration if applicable.  
   • Screen participants for caffeine sensitivity, cardiovascular contraindications, pregnancy, etc.  
   • Monitor vitals (heart rate, blood pressure) pre- and post- dosing; have emergency protocols in place.  
   • Ensure blind/randomization codes are securely held until data lock.
